title: Project Overview and Entry Point
description: aih-ui is the Policy Workbench user interface for AIH. It owns screens, interaction and presentation only. src/index.html holds the markup for every element on the page, and src/main.js is the entry point: it composes the app shell, the catalog feature and the governance feature and wires their callbacks together without holding any state itself. The README describes that composition and also lists what the repo must never contain: policy logic, catalog content or scanner execution.
languageLesson: src/main.js is a native ES module (loaded via <script type="module">). Vanilla JS with relative import specifiers means no bundler is needed; the browser resolves the module graph directly.

title: Repository Ground Rules
description: Before reading more code, learn the rules the code follows. AGENTS.md (which CLAUDE.md pulls in) says to build what prototype/ shows without redesigning it. It also says to use only the public interfaces of @aihq/core, @aihq/catalog and @aihq/scan, and to report a gap instead of copying logic. These rules explain why so many later modules are thin adapters and readers rather than engines.

title: Shared DOM and Absence Vocabulary
description: These two modules have the highest fan-in in the codebase: almost every component imports them. dom.js builds elements through textContent and looks up ids in a way that fails loudly, so package data is never parsed as HTML. absence.js defines one fixed set of words (Not published, Not declared, Not supplied, Not connected), so the UI never confuses a value that is missing with one that is empty or unavailable.
languageLesson: Setting textContent rather than innerHTML is the standard XSS-safe way to render untrusted strings in the DOM: the browser treats the value as literal text and never parses it as markup.

title: The App Shell
description: The first of main.js's direct dependencies is the application shell. shell.js owns the collapsible navigation and inspector rails, the inspector tabs and the error banner. theme.js repaints the page when the theme changes, and elements.js looks up the shell's DOM nodes once. The header controls in organization.js and ai-tools.js keep drafts local to the browser and never imply that anything was applied.

title: Catalog Controller and State
description: The Sources & Catalogs feature has one owner of state: catalog/controller.js holds the single selection and filter state and wires every catalog component through models and callbacks. index-source.js loads the served @aihq/catalog index and enforces its format and version contract. selectors.js computes every displayed count from that index at runtime, and view-state.js saves the view to sessionStorage and restores it.
languageLesson: Keeping state in one controller and passing callbacks down to stateless render functions is a framework-free form of unidirectional data flow, the same idea React popularised.

title: Reading Published Catalog Data
description: These modules are pure readers over what Catalog actually publishes. entry.js extracts identity, digests and labels from one entry. publisher.js, categories.js, qualification.js and collections.js attach Catalog's own presentation, category, qualification and collection records to index entries. They never infer a value Catalog did not publish, which is the AGENTS.md rule from Step 2 applied in code.

title: Catalog Renderers
description: Using the readers from Step 6 and the DOM helpers from Step 3, these components draw the Sources & Catalogs screen. They cover the card grid, the inspector's Details and Security tabs, the left-rail scopes, the filter toolbar and the six ledger metric tiles. Each one receives its data from the controller in Step 5 and never queries the DOM or holds state of its own.

title: Governance Controller and Transport
description: Governance is one vertical slice through @aihq/core: select a subject, inspect it, import evidence, prepare, save, reopen and consume. governance/controller.js runs that workflow. revisions.js guards every asynchronous answer with a revision token, so a verdict always reflects the current inputs. transport.js sends operator input unchanged to the preview backend's /api endpoints, and bytes.js carries artifacts as exact bytes in Base64.
languageLesson: Revision tokens are a common guard against race conditions with async/await: each request captures the current revision, and when the promise resolves the result is dropped if the revision has changed since.

title: Governance Pane Components
description: Each part of the Governance pane is a separate component that owns its own elements. inputs.js collects the subject, evidence and decision fields. prepared.js owns the Prepare step and the byte-exact downloads. reopen.js reloads those files in a fresh session, and verdict.js owns Consume and the verdict readout. statuses.js shows the six verification axes as six separate cells and never merges them into one badge.

title: Governance Wording Rules
description: The Governance pane controls its wording as strictly as its data. vocabulary.js defines the only words the pane may use, including the six status axes and refusal wording, and forbids terms such as Applied or Installed. rows.js is the single label/value renderer and shows null as an explicit absence word. detector.js keeps scanner attestation, scanner results and detector provenance as three separate statements.

title: The Preview Server
description: To see the page running, tools/preview.mjs builds a throwaway preview. packages.mjs resolves the three @aihq packages into tarballs, and preview.mjs installs them into a consumer and copies the page and service code in. The HTTP server then splits its work: api.mjs routes the /api/* calls that transport.js (Step 8) makes, and static.mjs serves files. preview-request.mjs classifies each URL, so malformed and path-traversal requests are refused.

title: Worker Process and Sessions
description: The server never imports the packages directly. service-client.mjs runs core-service.mjs as a child process inside the consumer and exchanges one JSON request for one JSON response. core-service.mjs then routes the request to a catalog, Core or validation operation. sessions.mjs derives every filesystem location from an opaque uuid, and artifacts.mjs handles byte-exact file I/O and names files by session-relative path.
languageLesson: The .mjs extension marks a file as an ES module in Node.js whatever package.json says. Running work in a child process over stdin/stdout isolates the installed packages from the server process.

title: Adapters over Published Packages
description: These adapters are the only code that touches @aihq/core, @aihq/catalog and @aihq/scan, and they use only the packages' public APIs. catalog-access.mjs reads installed Catalog content. catalog-served.mjs copies the reader's output into the served document member by member, so no field the reader dropped can reach the UI. core-adapter.mjs calls Core to derive subjects, prepare and consume, and scan-verifier.mjs enforces the operator's trust boundary. validation-fixture.mjs is the only module that creates test material, and it is labelled as validation mode.

title: The Prototype Design Source
description: prototype/ is the design the page must match. prototype/index.html is a clickable deck of the screens, and admin-sources.html is the owner's final Sources layout that the catalog feature follows. The shared tokens.css, tw-config.js and mode.js are loaded by src/index.html too (Step 1), so the real page and the prototype share the same colour roles, Tailwind setup and light/dark switching.
languageLesson: Design tokens as CSS custom properties (for example --color-surface) let one stylesheet switch themes by changing variable values under a .dark class. Tailwind's class-based darkMode reads the same class.

title: Contract and Acceptance Checks
description: The last stop is how the repo keeps these guarantees true. check-page-contract.mjs checks that every element id collected by the modules exists exactly once in src/index.html. acceptance-sweep.mjs replays the Governance call order against a running preview to confirm that no filesystem paths leak. The node:test suites pin specific behaviour, such as the served-catalog projection and the revision guard, and compare.html overlays the prototype on the page to check that the layouts match.
languageLesson: node:test is Node's built-in test runner (node --test). It provides describe/it/test and assert without any third-party dependency, which suits a repo that aims for zero build tooling.
